title.value: An Empirical Study of Retrieval-enhanced Graph Neural Networks
title.justification: The paper focuses on empirical studies and experimental evaluations of retrieval-enhanced graph neural networks, explicitly named in the abstract and throughout the paper.
title.quote: An effective approach to this challenge is to explicitly retrieve some annotated examples used to enhance GNN models.

extractions.description: The paper explores the enhancement of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) using a retrieval-based approach called Graph Retrieval. This method involves retrieving similar graph examples to augment GNN models for various graph property prediction tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements in GNN performance across multiple datasets, especially in addressing long-tailed label distribution problems.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on developing an enhanced methodology for graph neural networks rather than addressing any direct eco-responsible application related to climate change, sustainability, or natural systems protection.
primary_category.quote: To improve the representation power and performance of GNN models, existing studies mainly focus on the architecture design, and a growing plethora of new GNN models have been proposed.

secondary_categories.justification: While the paper itself does not directly address climate science, GNNs can be applied broadly to any domain involving graph-structured data, including environmental data modeling or climate science applications.
secondary_categories.quote: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are a class of neural architectures for supervised learning which has been adopted in a plethora of applications involving graph-structured data, such as molecular design, drug discovery, recommendation systems, and knowledge graph completion.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not specifically cater to any sub-category within an eco-responsible framework, focusing instead on technical improvements and empirical evaluations of GNNs.
primary_sub_category.quote: We have implemented our approach and used it to enhance three strong GNN backbone models, GCN, GIN, and PNA.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Despite not directly indicated in the paper, enhanced GNNs have the potential to be useful in climate modeling and prediction tasks where graph structures represent climate data.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are a class of neural architectures for supervised learning which has been adopted in a plethora of applications involving graph-structured data.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper is centered around improving graph neural network techniques by introducing retrieval-enhancement methods, which doesn't fit existing eco-responsible categories.
new_primary_category.quote: G RAPH R ETRIEVAL is a simple yet effective framework for enhancing graph neural networks.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: This sub-category addresses the specific enhancement discussed in the paper for GNNs handling long-tailed label distributions.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Moreover, our empirical study also illustrates that retrieval enhancement is a promising remedy for alleviating the long-tailed label distribution problem.
